rules.rule: Check for reversible causes during CPR
rules.problem: Trigger includes 'Absent pulse', whose descendants (any absent peripheral pulse) would fire it. Also check_for asks for thirst and dry mouth in a pulseless, unresponsive patient, which can't be elicited (footnote signs are history/exam of a conscious patient); page's other causes (trauma, diarrhoea/vomiting, glucose, temperature ≤ 35°C, overdose) are not checked, acceptable since no 'likely' diagnosis hangs on them.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tension pneumothorax during CPR
rules.problem: Structure (arrest AND any of unilateral hyperresonance / unilateral decreased breath sounds / deviated trachea) and 'probable' match the page. Only inherits the Absent pulse over-breadth.

Footnote 2 lists 'Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely' with no explicit any/all; OR-ing them means any single sign (e.g. dry mouth alone, or diastolic < 60 alone) gives probable dehydration — a loose reading. In a pulseless patient, thirst, dry mouth and BP cannot be assessed, so effectively only skin turgor applies. 'Thirst due to water deprivation' is narrower than the page.

Emergency level justified (no pulse/CPR). But 'Absent pulse' matches descendants such as 'Radial pulse absent', 'Femoral pulse absent' etc., so a patient with an absent limb pulse would be flagged Emergency/CPR. Replace with 'Carotid pulse absent' or Cardiac arrest only.

summary: Most consequential: 'Absent pulse' is used as a CPR/Emergency trigger in all four rules, but it subsumes 'Peripheral pulse absent' and every limb-pulse child, so an absent radial/femoral/pedal pulse would fire an Emergency CPR priority; use 'Carotid pulse absent' or Cardiac arrest. The dehydration rule ORs every footnote sign so one sign (incl. diastolic < 60 alone) gives probable dehydration, and thirst/dry mouth/BP are unassessable in a pulseless patient; 'Thirst due to water deprivation' is narrower than the page's 'Thirst' (use 'Increased thirst'). Tension pneumothorax rule is faithful.
